skill.name: automation-integration-preflight-action
skill.description: Evaluate a public webpage for automation and integration readiness through TinyOps x402 endpoints. Produce evidence-backed findings, prioritized integration risks, or an acceptance checklist without submitting forms or bypassing access controls.
skill.summary: Evaluate public webpages for automation readiness and integration risks with evidence from a TinyOps x402 service.
skill.author: tinyopsstudio

security_audit.summary: All 19 static findings are false positives caused by Markdown formatting, documented service URLs, protective credential prohibitions, or bounded API workflow instructions. No prompt injection or evidence of covert credential collection was found in SKILL.md. The workflow still requires careful user authorization because it can disclose a public target to a third-party service and initiate a paid request.

remediation.issue: The target URL and resulting page evidence are sent to a third-party TinyOps service.
remediation.suggestion: Document the service data-handling and retention terms, and remind users to submit only public, non-sensitive URLs.

remediation.issue: The workflow can initiate a paid x402 request.
remediation.suggestion: Keep live payment verification, exact purchase confirmation immediately before payment, and the one-request rule for ambiguous settlement or delivery.

remediation.issue: Literal URLs and Markdown code formatting trigger noisy static detections.
remediation.suggestion: No security change is required; retain the surrounding documentation that identifies these strings as API examples and safety restrictions.

content.value_statement: Teams need reliable evidence before investing in web automation or integrations. This skill checks public pages through TinyOps and returns readiness findings, risks, and acceptance guidance.
actual_capabilities: Inspect a public HTTP or HTTPS webpage without executing its JavaScript.
Request a TinyOps readiness analysis for a supplied public URL.
Request an acceptance pack with evidence, launch gates, acceptance tests, and prioritized remediation.
Verify live x402 payment requirements before a paid request.
Summarize readiness results, evidence, gaps, and practical next actions.
limitations: It does not inspect private or authenticated pages.
It does not submit forms, execute page JavaScript, or bypass access controls.
It requires user authorization and an already configured x402-capable payment client for paid requests.
It is not a vulnerability scanner or proof of end-to-end integration success.

use_cases.title: Preflight a SaaS Website
use_cases.description: Assess whether a public SaaS page exposes enough structure and evidence for a planned automation workflow.

use_cases.title: Prepare Launch Gates
use_cases.description: Generate evidence, acceptance tests, and prioritized gaps before approving a web-based integration.

use_cases.title: Evaluate a Prospect
use_cases.description: Review a public prospect website and identify practical automation constraints without requesting account access.

prompt_templates.title: Basic Readiness Check
prompt_templates.prompt: Check this public webpage for automation and integration readiness: [PUBLIC_URL]. Return the strongest evidence and the main gaps.

prompt_templates.title: Choose an Audit Mode
prompt_templates.prompt: Review [PUBLIC_URL]. Use a readiness analysis for a quick assessment, or an acceptance pack if launch gates and tests are needed. Explain the selected mode.

prompt_templates.title: Assess Launch Risk
prompt_templates.prompt: Evaluate [PUBLIC_URL] for a planned [WORKFLOW]. Identify evidence, integration risks, acceptance criteria, and prioritized next actions. Do not access private content.

prompt_templates.title: Authorize a Paid Audit
prompt_templates.prompt: For [PUBLIC_URL], inspect the public demo and live payment requirements first. Show the amount, asset, network, payee, and resource, then ask for confirmation before one exact paid request.

output_examples.output: Readiness: limited. Evidence: the page is publicly reachable and can be inspected without browser execution. Gaps: no workflow-specific acceptance evidence was established. Next action: define the target workflow and request an acceptance pack if launch gates are required.

output_examples.input: Create an acceptance pack for a public product page.
output: Evidence: public page observations and the selected integration context
Launch gates: explicit checks for required page structure and workflow behavior
Next actions: resolve prioritized gaps and confirm acceptance tests before launch

best_practices: Provide only a public URL and define the workflow you want to assess.
Verify the live payment amount, asset, network, payee, and resource before authorizing payment.
Separate observed page evidence from recommendations and preserve uncertainty in the final summary.
anti_patterns: Do not submit private, authenticated, credential-bearing, or secret-containing URLs.
Do not treat the result as a vulnerability scan or as proof that an integration works end to end.
Do not authorize payment from the published price alone or retry an ambiguous paid request automatically.

faq.question: What pages can this skill inspect?
faq.answer: It inspects public HTTP or HTTPS pages that do not require authentication or access-control bypasses.

faq.question: Does it execute JavaScript?
faq.answer: No. The workflow inspects the page without executing its JavaScript or submitting forms.

faq.question: What does the analysis endpoint provide?
faq.answer: It provides a readiness analysis with evidence-backed observations and prioritized integration risks.

faq.question: When should I request an acceptance pack?
faq.answer: Request one when you need evidence, launch gates, acceptance tests, and a prioritized remediation backlog.

faq.question: How are payments handled?
faq.answer: The skill verifies live x402 requirements and asks for confirmation immediately before using an authorized payment client.

faq.question: Can this prove my integration works?
faq.answer: No. It identifies readiness evidence and gaps, but it is not a vulnerability scanner or end-to-end integration test.
